You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Amazon Q2 Earnings Core: AWS 37% Growth Beats Expectations, Strongly Counters AI Spending Skepticism; Shares Surge Over 9% After Hours

TEXT:
Core Viewpoint
Amazon reported its second-quarter 2026 results, with revenue of $200.6 billion, up 20% year-over-year and above market expectations. AWS revenue reached $42.2 billion, up 37% year-over-year, significantly beating the expected approximately $40.6 billion and marking the fastest growth in 18 quarters. Both the AI business and custom chip business achieved annualized revenue run rates exceeding $25 billion, each growing at triple-digit percentages. The company raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance from $200 billion to $220 billion, while trailing twelve-month free cash flow turned negative at -$7.6 billion. Despite Q3 revenue and operating income guidance midpoints coming in below market expectations, the market overlooked the CapEx increase and negative free cash flow. Shares rose more than 9% in after-hours trading. The strong AWS growth effectively addressed prior skepticism over the returns on large-scale AI investments.
Detailed Breakdown
Overall Revenue and Profit Performance
Quarterly revenue: $200.6 billion, up 20% year-over-year, above market expectations.
Operating income: $27.5 billion, up 43% year-over-year, with an operating margin of 13.7%.
Net income: $62.6 billion, up 245% year-over-year; diluted EPS of $5.75. The sharp rise in net income was primarily driven by approximately $53.4 billion in pre-tax other income, mainly from investment gains related to Anthropic and other companies.
Total costs and expenses rose notably amid continued high AI-related investments.
Operating cash flow remained solid, but trailing twelve-month free cash flow recorded a net outflow of $7.6 billion, reaching a multi-year low.
AWS Cloud and AI Performance
AWS revenue: $42.2 billion, up 37% year-over-year (versus market expectations of approximately $40.6 billion), driving AWS annualized revenue to $169 billion and marking the fastest growth rate in 18 quarters.
AWS operating income: $16.6 billion, up 64% year-over-year, with operating margin rising to 39.4% (from 32.9% in the year-ago period).
AI business annualized revenue run rate exceeded $25 billion, with continued triple-digit year-over-year growth.
Custom AI chip business (Trainium and others) also exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate. Anthropic and OpenAI have both made multi-year, large-scale compute commitments.
Amazon Bedrock platform customer spend in the second quarter surpassed the combined total of all prior quarters. The platform now supports multiple foundation models, including those from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.
Other Business and Retail Metrics
North America sales: $116.2 billion, up 16% year-over-year.
International sales: $42.2 billion, up 15% year-over-year.
Advertising services revenue: $19.8 billion, up 26% year-over-year.
In the first half of the year, the number of same-day or next-day deliveries for Prime members increased by more than 40%. The second quarter included the annual Prime Day event, which supported consumer spending.
Capital Expenditure and Expense Plans
Full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance: raised from $200 billion to $220 billion, with the majority allocated to AI (data centers, servers, networking infrastructure, and custom chips).
The increase was driven primarily by higher memory chip costs and AI compute demand continuing to outstrip supply.
CEO Andy Jassy stated that even at the $220 billion level, Amazon will not have sufficient capacity to fully meet customer demand in 2026. He expects supply constraints to persist into 2027, with significant demand already locked in for 2028.
Second-quarter capital spending remained elevated, reflecting the ongoing acceleration of AI infrastructure buildout.
Next Quarter Guidance (Q3 2026)
Revenue guidance: $197 billion to $202 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 9% to 12%. The midpoint is below market expectations of approximately $203.9 billion.
Operating income guidance: $22.5 billion to $26.5 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 29% to 52%. The midpoint is also below market expectations.
Market Context and Investor Reaction
The core prior concern centered on whether rapid growth in AI capital expenditures would compress free cash flow and lead to overbuilding. Alphabet ’s shares came under pressure after it raised CapEx guidance, while Microsoft rose after holding its spending plans steady. Although Amazon raised CapEx and posted negative free cash flow, the 37% AWS growth beat demonstrated that the investments are translating into real demand and revenue, prompting a positive market response.
Investor reaction: Shares rose more than 9% in after-hours trading following the release. The market focused on the acceleration in AWS growth, the dual achievement of $25 billion+ annualized run rates for both AI and chip businesses, and signals of sustained strong compute demand.
Analyst perspective: The rebound in AWS growth provided strong support for the thesis that AI investments are beginning to generate returns, temporarily easing market concerns over heavy spending. Attention now turns to the pace of capacity deployment, actual Q3 results, and whether elevated memory costs will continue to push spending higher.
